sector_model: asset light consulting: P/E on GAAP and SBC-adjusted FCF, EV/sales, EBITDA margin, utilization, net cash, payout cover
thesis: Exponent (Nasdaq: EXPO) is a science and engineering consulting firm (failure analysis, user research, health and environmental) with about 950 consultants and no debt. Q3 FY26 (period ended 2026-10-02): total revenue 173.7M (+18%), revenue before reimbursements 153.1M (+12%), net income 30.9M ($0.64 vs $0.55), EBITDA margin 29.4% (28.3%), utilization 77%; nine months NI 89.9M (+10.7%), EPS 1.83 vs 1.58 (helped by a 4.4% lower diluted share count). FY guidance raised to revenue before reimbursements +10-11%, EBITDA margin 28.0-28.3%; Q4 +8-10%, margin 26.3-26.8%. Balance sheet 2026-10-02: cash 114.7M (down from 221.9M), no borrowings, equity 307.9M, total liabilities 387.0M mostly deferred comp, leases and payables. TTM FCF 140.6M (OCF 148.7M less capex 8.1M), 3.4% yield on 4.10B market cap (2.8% after 27.5M SBC). Close 86.22 on 2026-11-12: TTM GAAP EPS 2.32 gives 37.2x, EV/sales 6.0x, dividend 1.24 (1.4%). Nine month buybacks 146.1M at about 64.6 per share plus dividends 46.1M (192M) exceeded OCF 93.1M and drained cash by 107M. High quality, net cash and raised guidance, but the price already reflects it: no mispricing found.
counterthesis: At about 37x TTM earnings and 3% FCF yield after SBC the market pays a premium for steady mid-teens EBITDA growth; guidance implies Q4 growth slows to 8-10% and margin falls about 3 points year on year in guidance terms. Management repurchased shares at about 65 and now they trade 33% higher; payouts exceeded cash generation and cash fell by half, so buyback capacity is limited unless it borrows. Total revenue growth of 18% includes pass-through reimbursements; the underlying figure is 12%. Litigation and dispute demand is cyclical, utilization of 77% leaves little further margin gain, and 22M of SBC is a real cost. Peers, MD&A, segment margins, backlog-like indicators, concentration and the 10-K were not read.
invalidation: Attractive valuation would need a price near 20x earnings or evidence that earnings growth is far above guidance. Quality thesis fails if utilization falls below about 72%, revenue before reimbursements growth drops to low single digits, or the company borrows to fund repurchases.
